label: early-original-phase a/w/g/b/n input in sequences starting with 1/h/3/d/2/x
explanation: Fires only in the original (input) phase, never on the delimiter or during copying, and never at t=0/1. Activity is concentrated at t=2..5 (peak at t=3), with almost none at t>=7. The current input token matters most: a and w (about 6.5x lift), then g, b, n (3-4x); these five carry about 79% of activation mass. The prefix matters too: rates are much higher when the first token is 1 (5.5x), h, or 3 (about 3.8x), then d, 2, x, and when the token two steps back is 3/h/2/d. The top activations (0.9-1.0 of max) are a/w/g at t=3-4 in sequences beginning 1 h / 1 3 / 1 d. It looks like a conjunction of current token and early-prefix context, probably a hidden-state direction built up from many tokens, so no small predicate captures it cleanly. Restricting to sequences whose first token is one of those six gives dev F1 about 0.43 (precision 0.43, recall 0.43, mass recall 0.54). Activation mass rises with that coverage: the top quartile is covered best. Weak activations also occur on other tokens (j, v, o, e, l, z) and on repeated tokens.
